 with C.R.No.810/2023, dated 14/12/2023, registered with
 Malad Police Station, Mumbai, under sections 406, 420 r/w 34
 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: The FIR is lodged by one Ashishkumar Bafna.
He has
stated that he was an Advocate.

He was knowing one Vijay Patil,
 who told the informant that he could earn good profit if he  makes investment in the share market.
He gave reference of the  Applicant and his son Saurabh to the informant.
Vijay Patil  brought the Applicant and his son Saurabh to the informant's  office.
They had a discussion.

It is the case of the informant that  he was told that they were trading in Commodity trading and  Dabba Trading etc. and generally there was 20% profit on an  average and if the informant invested with them, he could gain  10% profit from that 20% profit.
They assured him to give profit  every month.
Based on this representation, the informant paid  Rs.1,13,20,000/- through cheque and Rs.17,80,000/- in cash  between 15/03/2021 to 16/06/2021.
He made total payment of  Rs.1,31,00,000/- in the account of 'Mylifetips' on t  instructions of the Applicant's son Saurabh.
According to him, he  had entered into an agreement dated 16/06/2021 with the  Applicant and his son.

It is further mentioned that on that date  the Applicant was not well and therefore his son Saurabh had  shown power of attorney given by him to his son Saurabh for ::: Uploaded on - 18/03/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 31/03/2024 03:22  3/7 902-ABA-533-24.odt  executing that agreement.

It is further mentioned that on that Chandrakant Balkrishna Mhatre vs State Of Maharashtra on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192708952/
2  date the stamp of Mylifetips Partnership Firm was not available  and therefore rubber stamp of Mylifetips Proprietor was used on  that agreement.

sentences.text: The FIR further mentions that Saurabh used to call the  informant time and again and used to tell him that they were  earning profit.
He returned only a comparatively small amount  i.e. Rs.3,23,500/-.
The other amount was not returned.
After  that, no amount was returned.
The Applicant and his son did not  make themselves available.
They have changed their residence.
On this basis, the FIR is lodged.
5. Learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that the  Applicant's name is included only to pressurize him.
The entire  representation was made by his son.
The amount was accepted  in the account of the partnership firm of the Applicant's son.
The  Applicant himself had absolutely no connection with any of the  transactions with Vijay and anybody else.

He submitted that the  Applicant is 68 years of age and his wife is suffering from ::: Uploaded on - 18/03/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 31/03/2024 03:22:59 ::
 4/7 902-ABA-533-24.odt  epileptic fits.
His son is absconding.
There is no one to look after  the Applicant and his wife.
He submitted that, on merits, there is  absolutely nothing against the present Applicant.
The allegations  are general, vague and false.
The Applicant has cooperated with  the investigation.
He has appeared before the police in the past.

sentences.text: He invited my attention to the say given by the investigating  agency before the Sessions Court in the proceedings of  Applicant's Anticipatory Bail Application.
It was clearly  mentioned in this say that the Applicant did not appear to have  any connection with Mylifetips, where the informant had  invested his amount.
6. Learned APP produced the investigation papers before  me.
He produced the copy of agreement between the Applicant  and his son Saurabh on one side and Vijay on the other.
That  copy contains signatures of two different persons for two  different entities.
One signature is made by the proprietor of  Mylifetips and the other signature is by the partner of Mylifetips.

Therefore apparently, there were two entities by the same name,

 7.
Learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that even  that signature is not made by the Applicant.
It is a forged  signature.
Learned APP submitted that this particular aspect is  still being investigated by inviting the opinion of the  handwriting expert.

sentences.text: Learned APP showed a copy of agreement between the  informant and both, the Applicant and his son.
However, on that  application, there were signatures of only one person i.e. the  proprietor of Mylifetips.
The FIR mentions that on that day, the  Applicant's son showed some power of attorney document  purportedly executed by the Applicant in favour of his son.
Based on that document, the said agreement was signed by  Saurabh and not by the Applicant.
9. Learned APP also produced certain statements  recorded after 02/03/2024.
Those statements are recorded after ::: Uploaded on - 18/03/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 31/03/2024 03:22:59   6/7 902-ABA-533-24.odt
the matter was argued in this Court on 26/02/2024.
Learned  counsel for the Applicant submitted that those statements are  recorded only to overcome the submissions made by the  Applicant on that particular date before the Court.
I have  perused these statements and even in those statements there is  only a general allegation that the Applicant had accompanied  his son to the office of the investor.
Beyond that, there is nothing  to show that the Applicant himself had accepted any amount in  his account.
10. I have considered these submissions.
Considering this  discussion, I find that there is substance in the submissions of  the learned counsel for the Applicant.

sentences.text: The Applicant is 68 years of age and his wife is  suffering from health issues as mentioned earlier.

In this  background and also taking into account the say filed by the  investigating agency, before the Sessions Court, at this stage, the  Applicant can be protected by way of ad-interim relief till the ::: Uploaded on - 18/03/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 31/03/2024 03:22:59 :::
 7/7 902-ABA-533-24.
 next date.
The Applicant will have to cooperate with the  investigation.

11 . Hence, the following order :
 ORDER (i) In the event of his arrest in connection with C.R.No.810/2023, dated 14/12/2023, registered with Malad Police Station, Mumbai, till the next date, the Applicant is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing PR bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one or two sureties in the like amount.
(ii) The Applicant shall attend the concerned Police Station as and when called and shall cooperate with the investigation.
(iii) This order shall operate till 23/04/2024.
(iv) Stand over to 23/04/2024.

(SARANG V. KOTWAL, J.)
